_doc: The general classifier a language counts with, by ISO 639-3.
WALS 55A says whether a language needs one and the profile has carried
that answer all along -- a derived grammar even announces 'numeral
classifiers obligatory' in its notes -- but nothing ever wrote one, so
Mandarin counted 三立方體 where 三个立方体 is the language.
Only the general classifier, and only where the numeral and the noun sit
either side of it in the order the profile already knows: Mandarin and
Cantonese and Vietnamese put Num-CLF-N, Thai and Bengali N-Num-CLF, and
both fall out of WALS 89A without anything further.
Japanese and Korean are absent deliberately. Both need a classifier and
both place it in ways this parameter cannot express -- Japanese floats
the numeral away from its noun entirely -- so writing one in would put a
real word in the wrong place, which is worse than the gap.
A language WALS marks 'optional' is absent too. Optional means the bare
numeral is grammatical, and it is the one this engine can already write.
The numeral and the classifier are joined by the language's own word
joiner, so Chinese and Thai write them together and Vietnamese apart.
Bengali is absent for the same reason Japanese is: its classifier is an
enclitic on the numeral rather than a word beside it, and this parameter
cannot say so.
